blocks.text: Model evaluation is a process of checking how well a machine learning model performs. It measures the quality of predictions made by the model using test data that was not used during training. This helps in identifying the strengths and weaknesses of the model. Performance metrics are measures used to evaluate how well a model is working. Different metrics are used depending on the type of problem, discussed below:

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text: A model with high accuracy may still give wrong results in some cases. That is why other measures like precision and recall are used. Proper evaluation helps understand the real performance of a model.

Accuracy shows how many predictions are correct out of the total predictions. It is measured as a percentage. High accuracy means better performance. The error shows incorrect predictions. Error rate is the opposite of accuracy. Accuracy alone may be misleading sometimes. Balanced data gives better accuracy results. Error analysis helps find mistakes. Both measures are important for evaluation. The accuracy equation is:

items: TP (True Positives): Number of correctly predicted positive instances.
TN (True Negatives): Number of correctly predicted negative instances.
FP (False Positives): Number of incorrectly predicted positive instances.
FN (False Negatives): Number of incorrectly predicted negative instances.

blocks.text: Precision measures how many predicted positive results are actually correct. Recall measures how many actual positive cases are correctly identified. Precision focuses on correctness. Recall focuses on completeness. High precision reduces false results. High recall reduces missed cases.

items: TP (True Positives): Correctly predicted positive instances.
FP (False Positives): Incorrectly predicted positive instances.
TP (True Positives): Correctly predicted positive instances.
FN (False Negatives): Incorrectly predicted negative instances.

blocks.text: F1-score is the balance between precision and recall. It gives a single performance score. F-measure is useful when the data is unbalanced. It balances correctness and completeness. A higher F-measure means better performance. It avoids relying on accuracy alone. F1-score is commonly used in evaluation. It gives a fair comparison.

items: Precision: The proportion of positive predictions that are actually correct.
Recall: The proportion of actual positive instances that are correctly identified.

blocks.title: Example:
blocks.problem: Suppose we are given the following values: TP (True Positives) = 40; TN (True Negatives) = 50; FP (False Positives) = 10; FN (False Negatives) = 5. Now, let's calculate Precision, Recall, and F1-Score based on these values.
